newsitem.title: USA: U.S WCoast crudes drop on late NYMEX profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: U.S WCoast crudes drop on late NYMEX profit-taking.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude prices dropped as profit-taking in NYMEX heating oil followed reports of increased distillate stocks.
November heating oil on NYMEX settled 2.22 cents lower at 73.97 cents a gallon, with distillates up a higher-than-expected 1.3 million barrels last week.
Buyers and sellers remained widely apart, with refiners cowed by poor profits and higher futures prices.
Buyers also held back on news that a cargo of Canadian Koch Alberta was offered for loading in mid-November.
They bid for the 500,000 barrel cargo of Koch Alberta -- a 34 API gravity grade which competes with Alaskan grades.
The cargo was offered because testing last month on a major Canadian pipeline left extra reserves of light crude.
Bids were seen around $2.50 a barrel less November WTI, while offers stayed $2.10.
November West Texas Intermediate (WTI) fell 45 cents late to $24.95/25.05 a barrel.
Outright prices for Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude prices dropped to $22.55/22.85 a barrel.
The discount for Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude remained $2.30 a barrel less November West Texas Intermediate (WTI).
Line 63 diffs remained unchanged at $3.20 to $3.00 under spot WTI for November delivery.
Kern River, from California's San Joaquin Valley, rose with postings to 16.80/17.00 a barrel.
And prices for Long Beach-based Wilmington crude also tracked higher postings to $18.15/18.25 a barrel.
